summary: Tehama County, CA lookout site used since at least 1922; state cabin built 1937 was gone by 1986; parcel listed for possible sale in 2014. No current site description found.

facts.design: 8x8 foot wood-frame observation cabin on a 60-foot treated timber tower (1937), with a BC-201 residence cabin
facts.status_note: Register says the lookout structure was gone by 1986; no source describes what remains today

events.note: Earliest documented use. Register says a lookout has been here since at least 1922; a 1922 newspaper report has a ranger sighting a fire from the station
Brush fire in the Polk Springs district; the man who admitted starting it pleaded guilty and was fined $50; about 800 acres burned Plea dated May 3, 1922.
Register: State of California built a new 8x8 foot observation cabin on a 60 foot treated timber tower, plus a BC-201 residence cabin
2011 Assembly analysis: CAL FIRE acquired the property in 1971 to construct a fire lookout tower. Conflicts with the register's 1937 state build date
Register Removed field reads 'Pre 1986'; description says the structure was gone by 1986. Year is an upper bound
AB 1272 (enrolled) would authorize the director to dispose of the parcel, described as about 5 acres; April 2011 analysis says about 20 acres

corrections.why: Register Removed field reads 'Pre 1986' and the description says the structure was gone by 1986; 1986 is an upper bound, not a removal date

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The April 2011 Assembly analysis says about 20 acres; the enrolled bill (July 2011, later) says about 5 acres. The enrolled text is used for the parcel size and both figures are reported in the story.

The register says the state built a structure in 1937; the 2011 analysis says CAL FIRE acquired the property in 1971 to construct a lookout. The sources do not reconcile these dates, so the story reports both.

sources.title: AB 1272, State property: surplus (enrolled bill text)

notes_for_editor: Brief's 2020 registration date (Dec 12, 2020) is not in the cached register page (Date Registered value is blank), so it is left out. The 1922 newspaper quotes come secondhand via a volunteer site that quotes the Red Bluff Daily News; verify against the original paper if possible. Calisphere 1938 photo page returned no text and is not used. Access is not established by any source read, so no access key is recorded; the 2014 parcel status is the latest fact found. The 1922 quotes spell the name 'Campbelville'; the register and bill use 'Campbellville'. Height_m is the 60-foot tower height as stated, converted to metres.
